Multi-Scale Embodied Intelligence Lab.title: Spatial-Spectral Coupling as Attention: Scaling Shape Correspondence to High-Resolution Surfaces
Multi-Scale Embodied Intelligence Lab.authors_text: Bence Demeter, Kilian Ehrenreich, Amelie Kleber, Ioana Oprisiu, Philipp Spohn
Multi-Scale Embodied Intelligence Lab.summary: The paper introduces Geo-FlashAttention, an efficient attention mechanism that scales shape correspondence for high-resolution 3D surfaces, improving runtime and memory while preserving accuracy.
Multi-Scale Embodied Intelligence Lab.debug_abstract: Establishing dense correspondence between high-resolution 3D shapes remains challenging due to the spatial--spectral coupling at the core of many functional-map methods, which grows quadratically with mesh resolution. We observe that this coupling is equivalent to a scaled dot-product attention formulation, with learned descriptors serving as queries and keys and spectral basis functions as values. This connection makes efficient attention implementations directly applicable to shape matching and an effective mechanism for scaling spatial-spectral coupling. We show that optimized quadratic attention implementations can scale modern deep functional map pipelines to large mesh sizes, improving both runtime and memory consumption, while sub-quadratic methods introduce errors, particularly for non-isometric shape pairs, where an exact coupling proves most necessary. These insights motivate \textit{Geo-FlashAttention}, which restricts the exact softmax to geometry-selected surface patches and achieves near-linear empirical scaling while preserving correspondence accuracy of exact implementations. Across six standard benchmarks and three functional-map pipelines, rigorous analysis shows that efficient couplings preserve correspondence accuracy. At $60k$ vertices, these insights reduce peak training memory from 106.08 to 5.67\,GiB, with Geo-FlashAttention being $1.5\times$ faster per training step than FlashAttention. This enables end-to-end learning for correspondence problems on large meshes such as cortical surfaces, where high resolution is required to preserve disease-relevant intricacies of the surface geometry. Project page available https://spatial-spectral-attention.github.io/

Multi-Scale Embodied Intelligence Lab.title: RaMOD: Moving-Object Detection from Raw mmWave Radar Cubes under Ego Motion
Multi-Scale Embodied Intelligence Lab.authors_text: Yuan Fang, Long Zhuang, Lingzi Xing, Xijia Wei, Jingqi Jiang
Multi-Scale Embodied Intelligence Lab.summary: RaMOD is a real-time framework that enhances moving-object detection and velocity estimation from raw mmWave radar cubes by addressing ego motion and Doppler wrapping challenges.
Multi-Scale Embodied Intelligence Lab.debug_abstract: Millimeter-wave (mmWave) radar provides weather-robust sensing and direct Doppler measurements, yet automotive perception pipelines often reduce its output to sparse point clouds or two-dimensional projections, leaving raw range-azimuth-Doppler (RAD) cubes underutilized. Ego motion induces Doppler responses from world-static structures, while Doppler wrapping aliases radial velocities, complicating moving-object detection and velocity estimation. We present RaMOD (Radar-based Moving-Object Detection), a real-time framework for moving-object detection and velocity estimation from raw RAD cubes acquired by a vehicle-mounted single-chip radar. RaMOD explicitly estimates frame-wise ego motion and uses the estimated radar translational velocity to predict the Doppler region of world-static structures and suppress returns within it. It temporally encodes the suppressed cubes into multi-scale features to predict RAD-space boxes with class labels. For each detected object, it predicts radial and forward velocities under raw-Doppler and Doppler-unwrapped hypotheses, together with Doppler-wrapping probabilities. On our BRIDGE-Liv dataset, RaMOD outperforms all compared raw-radar methods across RAD-cube, RA, and RD detection settings, achieving 80.8% cube mAP at IoU 0.30, 15.7 percentage points above the strongest RAD-cube baseline. Velocity MAE is 1.128 m/s, with 99.87% Doppler-wrapping accuracy.

北京航空航天大学.title: XS-VLA: Teaching Tiny Vision-Language-Action Models with Spatial Supervision and Demonstration Conditioning
北京航空航天大学.authors_text: Iok Tong Lei, Ying Jie Yap, Wei Huang, Qingchen Xie, Qianzhi Li
北京航空航天大学.summary: XS-VLA enhances robot control efficiency by using spatial supervision and demonstration conditioning, achieving significant performance improvements while maintaining a compact model size.
北京航空航天大学.debug_abstract: How can richer training supervision improve robot control while keeping the deployed policy compact? We present XS-VLA, a staged training framework using teacher-derived spatial labels and demonstration-conditioned action learning. Coarse-Grained Spatial Distillation (CSD) initializes the backbone through an auxiliary region-label task. Latent Flow Matching (LFM) then conditions an action-space velocity field on a demonstration latent, using KL regularization while jointly optimizing the backbone and action modules. The deployed policy contains 243.99M parameters and operates without the teacher or posterior encoder. XS-VLA achieves 90.25% average LIBERO success in each of two training seeds, compared with 86.00% for a SmolVLA-0.25B base trained under our settings. Ablations examine both training stages through matched image pretraining and Huber/MSE controls. On three Mobile ALOHA tasks, average strict success increases from 21.7% to 65.0%. These results demonstrate the control utility of auxiliary representation initialization and regularized demonstration-conditioned flow learning for compact VLA policies

具身智能多模态大模型中心.title: A Comprehensive Survey of Agent Distillation across Models, Artifacts, and Harnesses
具身智能多模态大模型中心.authors_text: Ziluowen Luo, Senzhang Wang, Chaozhuo Li, Jun Yin, Hao Yan
具身智能多模态大模型中心.summary: This paper presents a unified survey on Agent Distillation, emphasizing persistent knowledge transfer across models, artifacts, and harnesses to enhance agent capabilities and adaptability.
具身智能多模态大模型中心.debug_abstract: Knowledge distillation provides a teacher-student framework for transferring capabilities at reduced cost and has been widely studied for large language models (LLMs). As LLM-based agents move from response generation to sustained, closed-loop task solving, distillation expands beyond model parameters to knowledge retained in reusable resources and execution workflows. This shift from model-level to agent-level knowledge transfer supports efficient deployment, broader capability access, and continual self-evolution. However, existing surveys largely examine model distillation and agent system design separately, limiting comparison of transfer strategies across agent components. To bridge this gap, we formalize Agent Distillation as persistent knowledge transfer between teacher and student agents and present its first unified survey. Distinguishing experience used for transfer from knowledge retained for reuse, we develop a knowledge-substrate taxonomy based on where knowledge persists: models, artifacts, or harnesses. Building on this taxonomy, we analyze cross-substrate transfer paths and hybrid strategies. To assess the resulting capabilities, we review benchmarks and evaluation protocols for retention, causal attribution, and deployed utility without further teacher support. This survey provides a unified basis for studying agent knowledge transfer and developing efficient, adaptable, and self-evolving agents.

上海人工智能实验室.title: $A^3$-VLA: Automatic Perception-Guided Attention Alignment for Robot Manipulation
上海人工智能实验室.authors_text: Shengzhe Zhang, Qi Zhang, Dazhong Shen, Chao Wang, Shaopeng Zhai
上海人工智能实验室.summary: The $A^3$-VLA framework enhances robot manipulation by integrating task-specific visual guidance, improving attention alignment and performance in Vision-Language-Action models.
上海人工智能实验室.debug_abstract: Vision-Language-Action Models (VLAs) enable robots to perform manipulation tasks by leveraging Vision-Language Models (VLMs) to process visual observations and language instructions. However, the action prediction objective itself lacks fine-grained task-specific perceptual supervision, making it prone to relying on task-irrelevant visual shortcuts, leading attention away from target objects and key interaction areas, thereby limiting its operational performance and generalization ability. To address this, we propose Automatic Perception-Guided Attention Alignment for Robot Manipulation ($A^3$-VLA), a framework that derives task-specific visual guidance from the manipulation process itself. Specifically, $A^3$-VLA first generates heuristic candidate regions for target objects and the robot from interaction-induced visual changes, and refines them with a visual segmentation model offline. These regions serve as explicit perceptual guidance through two complementary objectives: an attention allocation loss that encourages sufficient focus on task-critical regions when language or robot state tokens query the visual input, and a contrastive learning loss that aligns the representations of candidate target regions with language instructions while separating them from task-irrelevant regions. Extensive experiments on simulated and real-world manipulation tasks demonstrate that $A^3$-VLA consistently improves multiple VLA backbones, with an average success rate gain of 6.5% - 25.2% across benchmarks.

西湖机器人科技 / 机器智能实验室 (MiLAB).title: ODEAction: From Predicting Chunks to Evolving Actions
西湖机器人科技 / 机器智能实验室 (MiLAB).authors_text: Qishen Wang, Pengxiang Ding, Shifeng Bao, Mingyang Sun, Hengtao Li
西湖机器人科技 / 机器智能实验室 (MiLAB).summary: ODEAction introduces a continuous action evolution framework using ODEs to enhance vision-language-action models, improving task performance and trajectory quality over traditional chunk-based methods.
西湖机器人科技 / 机器智能实验室 (MiLAB).debug_abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models typically generate actions in chunks, dividing continuous robot execution into separately predicted action chunks, which can introduce discontinuities at chunk boundaries. We propose ODEAction, a chunk-free action generation paradigm that replaces action chunk prediction with Continuous Action Evolution. We use an ordinary differential equation (ODE) to describe the continuous evolution of actions, and define the vector field of this ODE as the Action Transition Field to characterize how actions evolve with respect to evolution time. During inference, the model takes the current action as the initial condition and numerically solves the ODE defined by the learned Action Transition Field, thereby recursively generating subsequent actions with explicit dependencies. ODEAction is implemented as a modular action head that can be integrated with different vision-language backbones. Experiments on LIBERO, EBench, RoboTwin, and real-robot tasks show that, compared with action-chunk-based baselines, ODEAction improves both task performance and trajectory quality, with particularly pronounced gains on fine manipulation tasks.
